etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/kono aida/ → /konaida/
Contraction of このあいだ (kono aida, “recently, the other day”).
First cited in 1563.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
This etymology is hypothetical. Possibly some kind of sound shift from 順当 (juntō, “properly, in a smooth way”).
/dʑɯntoː/ → /dʑɯnto/ → /tɕanto/

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Ultimately from Latin Āfrica.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Shortened from earlier ハンバーグステーキ (hanbāgu sutēki), a borrowing from English Hamburg steak.
First cited to 1941.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Borrowed from English Hamburg.
First cited to 1898.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Sense 1 is from English rule.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From tei (定, fixed) + ka (価, monetary value).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 小(こ) (ko-, “little”) + 麦(むぎ) (mugi, “dry-cultivated cereal grain”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/wo/ → /o/
From Old Japanese 尾 (wo), from Proto-Japonic *bo.
First attested in the Kojiki of 712 CE in the senses “tail” and “foot of a mountain”.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 尾 (MC mj+jX).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/arasi/ → /araɕi/
From Old Japanese.
Derivation theories include:
* Compound of 荒ら (ara, “desolate, sparse”, archaic) + 風 (shi, “wind”, obsolete).
* From 荒らし (arashi, “destroyer”), the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of verb 荒らす (arasu, “destroy, ruin”).
* Apophonic form of 颪 (oroshi, “wind blowing down from the mountains”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/ram/ → /ramʉ/ → /ran/
From Middle Chinese 嵐 (MC lom).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 帰(き) (ki, “return”) + 宅(たく) (taku, “home”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 恐(きょう) (kyō, “awful, fear”) + 縮(しゅく) (shuku, “shrink”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
手 (shu, “hand”) + 術 (-jutsu, “technique”).
Presumably a Meiji period calque of Ancient Greek χειρουργία (kheirourgía).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 持(も)ち (mochi, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 持(も)つ (motsu, “to hold”)) + 上(あ)げる (ageru, “to raise, to lift”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 新 (“new”) + 幹線 (“main line”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Orthographic borrowing from Chinese 歌謠／歌谣 (gēyáo).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 死 is a daiyōji replacing 屍.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 演 ("perform," "put on") + 奏 ("play (music)").

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese, in turn from Proto-Japonic *tumay. The standalone form of tsuma below.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese. The root form of tsume above, generally only used in compounds. Cognate with 端 (tsuma, “edge, side of something”) and 妻 (tsuma, “wife”, original sense of “spouse”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Cognate with 成る (naru, “become”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 異 (MC yiH). Compare modern Mandarin 異 /异 (yì, /i⁵¹/), Cantonese 異 /异 (ji⁶, /jiː²²/).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 稅 (MC sywejH). First cited in Japanese to a portion of the Shoku Nihongi dated to 719.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Shift in sense from 力 (chikara, “strength”), implying "that which is produced from strength".
First cited in the 延喜式 (Engishiki) of 927.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *tanay.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese.
Possibly derived from or cognate with 草(くさ) (kusa, “grass”), from the way grass grows from its base, hence origin.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨kusa papi₁⟩ → * /kusapapʲi/ → /kusafafi/ → /kusawawʲi/ → /kusawai/
Compound of 種(くさ) (kusa, “origin; type”) + 這(は)い (hai, “widely spread out”, the 連用形(れんようけい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of 這(は)う (hau, “to spread out widely”)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/t͡ɕɨu/ → /ɕʲu/ → /ɕu/
From Middle Chinese 種 (MC tsyowngX).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 空 (kū, “air, sky”) + 港 (kō, “port”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 茶色(ちゃいろ) (chairo) + い (-i).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: /kagapuru/ → /kagaɸuru/.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Contraction of 被る (kagafuru). The medial -g- voices /p/ to /b/.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 被る (kaburu). Bilabial plosive /b/ becomes bilabial nasal /m/.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: /kagapuru/ → /kauburu/ → /koːburu/.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 被る (kōburu). Bilabial plosive /b/ becomes bilabial nasal /m/.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 言葉 (“word”) + 遣い (“way of using”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/kimʉ/ → /kiɴ/
From Middle Chinese 金 (kim). Compare modern Mandarin 金 (jīn), Hokkien 金 (kim).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/komʉ/ → /koɴ/
From Middle Chinese 金 (kim).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese.
Possibly derived from unbound prefix kana- fused with い (i, nominal particle).
The four kanji spellings of this term, 金 (“gold”), 銀 (“silver”), 銅 (“copper”), and 鉄 (“iron”), hint at the importance of each of these four metals in ancient Japan.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese, ultimately from Proto-Japonic *kankay. Cognate with 影(かげ) (kage, “shadow”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 陰 (ʔˠiɪm).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/hoto₂/: *[potə] → [ɸoto] → [hoto].
As indicated in the Wamyōshō citation, /to₂/ may be related to 処(と) (/to₁/, “place, location”), but the phonological difference can not be explained. Perhaps related to Korean 보지 (boji, “vagina”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 雑 (“miscellaneous”) + 音 (“sound”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 飢 is a daiyōji replacing 饑.
